Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,

background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. You may instead reply
SELECT n to submit a previously successful execution step n shown in feedback. Otherwise
the last successful build is submitted automatically. Budget includes planning, corrections
and review calls: at most 5 fresh CLI sessions, 3 Blender executions and 1200 seconds.
Do not invoke tools, other models, hidden agents or additional executions yourself.

Procedure:
Make the first build a complete, economical reconstruction, with all large visible objects,
recognizable silhouettes, broad materials and lighting. Estimate several normalized image
landmarks (x/width, y/height from top left), including subject extremes, contact points and
architectural intersections. Record estimates and uncertainties in short code comments.
Use perspective and visible edge directions to choose camera position and orientation;
use image occupancy to refine framing. Keep focal length, camera pose, object dimensions,
placement and light strengths as explicit parameters. Match cropped foreground objects
and negative spaces as well as central objects. Do not assume every photograph is level,
centered, symmetric or taken from a standard viewpoint.

Plan the first scene by visible assemblies and filled image regions. Distinguish solid
panels, upholstery, rails and true openings: a perimeter of rods does not replace a broad
solid apron, panel or cushion. Preserve the visible thickness and internal negative spaces
that make the main silhouettes recognizable. Include small but conspicuous occluders and
cropped objects before repetitive decoration. Avoid regularizing irregular silhouettes
merely because boxes and tubes are convenient.

Budget expanded geometry, not source-code length. sweep_tube with N points emits N balls
and N-1 rods. fillet_box can emit 23 meshes. Repeated long tube paths and broad fields of
individual boards can dominate realization time despite a short render timing line.
Initially aim for a few hundred emitted meshes, roughly 300-400 when practical. This is
an economy heuristic, not a hard limit or reason to omit major visible objects. Use about
6-10 points for ordinary curved members initially, increasing only where visible curvature
requires it. Use procedural materials for fine weave, grain and repeated surface seams.
Keep silhouettes and meaningful editable components as geometry. Do not merge unrelated
objects to meet a count. Avoid generating large decorative fields outside the visible area.

After an actual render, compare framing, visible object coverage, silhouette, occlusion and
broad tone before fine detail. Record a few approximate reference/render landmark pairs,
the largest supported discrepancy, a proposed parameter family and its expected image
movement, plus two matching regions to preserve. Do not present visual estimates as exact
measurements. Correct missing solid regions or wrong openings before adding ornament.
A coherent displacement or slope error across multiple objects suggests a camera correction;
an isolated silhouette or occlusion error suggests local geometry/placement correction.
Perspective, distance, focal length and scale are ambiguous from one image: use multiple
landmarks and background alignment, not just one object's size. Prefer one coherent change
family per revision, allowing directly necessary dependent changes. Do not change focal
length, camera distance and whole-object scale to compensate for the same error. Do not
raise several objects to disguise an unsupported camera-pitch choice. Preserve plausible
support and relative placement as well as image alignment. Adjust broad lighting or finish
only with a stated regional reason; avoid simultaneously darkening all materials, lights
and exposure without checking already matching regions.

Revision time includes model generation, scene construction, saving and rendering. The
policy uses observed complete execution wall time to reserve time for a useful revision.
When instructed to select only, return SELECT n; do not write an unexecutable final revision.

- include(name, node) REPLACES an existing child with that name. Use unique keys within
  each parent, especially in loops. Layout functions return copies; attach their results.

  Include all constituent surfaces and supports in the corresponding assembly. Do not
  change names to affect an evaluator's target selection. An edit pass on one selected

  sc = bpy.context.scene
  if sc.world is None: sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('AmbientWorld')
  sc.world.use_nodes = True

  parent's mesh descendants, or set primitive node.name explicitly before realize.
  Copy shared materials before changing only one object's finish.

  materials for subpixel surface texture. Geometry should express visible shape, structure
  and editable parts. Many meshes alone do not establish semantic completeness.
- AABB anchors are world-axis bounds, not surface contact or collision tests. Use explicit
  pivots for intended rotations and check plausible support and occlusion in the image.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='center', target_anchor=None, offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
For an Asset target, omitted target_anchor uses source_anchor. For a world-point target,
omit target_anchor. To put a bottom on a top, specify both anchors explicitly.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='center',target_anchor='center',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
Use explicit bottom/top anchors for support. Constraint endpoints cannot be ancestors or
 descendants of each other, and bindings must be acyclic.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

import bpy, math, random
from mathutils import Vector
from sceneact import *

# Assemblies: paneled cream wall, parquet floor, left curtains, carved chaise,
# loose pillow, green seat label, and a cropped cane chair at lower left.
# Approximate image landmarks: head crown (.09,.25), seat/head junction (.36,.49),
# foot (.82,.70), front feet (.33,.84), (.78,.94), wall/floor corner (.91,.50).
# Upholstered head and side wings are FILLED panels; space below the apron is open.
# Uncertain: hidden rear feet, head curvature, and wall distance behind the chaise.

random.seed(12)
LENGTH, WIDTH, SEAT_Z = 2.65, 1.02, .67
CAMERA = (3.15, -5.4, 3.65)
TARGET = (-.08, .03, .89)
LENS = 47
FRAME = (.40, .46, .38)
EDGE = (.63, .63, .48)
CREAM = (.78, .74, .63)
WALL = (.70, .68, .60)

scene = Scene('French chaise interior')
architecture = Asset('Architecture')
architecture.include('floor', box((12, 12, .12), center=(0, 0, -.07),
                                  color=(.20, .105, .058)))
architecture.include('back_wall', box((10, .16, 4), center=(0, 1.12, 2), color=WALL))
architecture.include('right_pilaster', box((.43, .42, 3.4),
                     center=(2.17, .96, 1.7), color=(.75, .74, .67)))

def trim(name, size, pos, color=CREAM):
    architecture.include(name, box(size, center=pos, color=color))

for z, depth, height in [(.08,.12,.16),(.21,.09,.055),(.28,.065,.035),
                         (1.64,.055,.045),(1.72,.075,.04),(1.91,.045,.025),
                         (2.13,.065,.04)]:
    trim('horizontal_'+str(z), (8, depth, height), (0,1.005-depth/2,z))
# Broad rectangular raised wall molding.
for x in [-1.91, 1.91]:
    trim('panel_side_'+str(x), (.027,.035,1.20), (x,1.005,.96))
    trim('panel_side_inner_'+str(x), (.012,.045,1.12), (x + (.043 if x<0 else -.043),.988,.96))
for z in [.36,1.56]:
    trim('panel_edge_'+str(z), (3.83,.035,.028), (0,1.005,z))
for z in [.40,1.52]:
    trim('panel_inner_'+str(z), (3.74,.042,.013), (0,.992,z))
trim('pilaster_inner', (.024,.025,2.3), (2.07,.733,1.60))
scene.include('architecture', architecture)

chaise = Asset('Chaise_longue')
# Solid carved apron below the upholstery.
chaise.include('front_apron', box((2.38,.075,.18), center=(.03,-.502,.535),color=FRAME))
chaise.include('back_apron', box((2.38,.065,.15), center=(.03,.49,.55),color=FRAME))
chaise.include('foot_apron', box((.08,.91,.16),center=(1.25,0,.54),color=FRAME))

def tube(parent, name, pts, radius, color):
    parent.include(name, sweep_tube(points=pts,radius=radius,color=color))

# Short, continuous cabriole paths with outward feet.
for x in [-1.00,1.17]:
    for y in [-.46,.43]:
        s = -1 if x<0 else 1
        t = -1 if y<0 else 1
        pts=[(x,y,.55),(x+.025*s,y+.018*t,.44),
             (x-.025*s,y+.035*t,.29),(x-.045*s,y+.06*t,.11),
             (x+.01*s,y+.09*t,.045)]
        tube(chaise,'leg_'+str(x)+'_'+str(y),pts,.039,FRAME)
        tube(chaise,'leg_gilt_'+str(x)+'_'+str(y),
             [(p[0],p[1]-.033,p[2]) for p in pts],.008,EDGE)

# Upholstered front wing rises steeply into the left head.
wing_outline=[(-1.37,.64),(-1.43,1.34),(-1.32,1.43),(-1.15,1.29),
              (-.99,1.16),(-.81,1.04),(-.65,.96),(-.54,.83),
              (-.53,.61),(-.73,.51),(-1.12,.53)]
for y in [-.515,.48]:
    pts=[(x,y,z) for x,z in wing_outline]
    tube(chaise,'wing_border_'+str(y),pts+[pts[0]],.031,FRAME)
    tube(chaise,'wing_beading_'+str(y),
         [(x,y-.025,z+.009) for x,z in wing_outline]+
         [(wing_outline[0][0],y-.025,wing_outline[0][1]+.009)],.008,EDGE)

# Head frame across the width, with an irregular arched crown.
head_top=[(-1.40,-.50,1.34),(-1.43,-.38,1.58),(-1.44,-.18,1.69),
          (-1.43,.06,1.70),(-1.39,.30,1.62),(-1.34,.48,1.48)]
tube(chaise,'head_crown',head_top,.038,FRAME)
tube(chaise,'head_crown_bead',[(x+.022,y,z+.018) for x,y,z in head_top],.009,EDGE)
for y in [-.50,.48]:
    tube(chaise,'head_post_'+str(y),
         [(-1.32,y,.50),(-1.37,y,.86),(-1.41,y,1.24),(-1.40,y,1.48)],.035,FRAME)
# Upholstery-edge piping along the long seat.
for y in [-.51,.51]:
    tube(chaise,'seat_piping_'+str(y),
         [(-1.09,y,.72),(-.55,y,.73),(.25,y,.73),(1.06,y,.72),(1.29,y*.85,.69)],.011,EDGE)
tube(chaise,'apron_lower_bead',
     [(-1.13,-.548,.49),(-.70,-.548,.47),(-.23,-.548,.48),
      (.20,-.548,.46),(.72,-.548,.48),(1.22,-.51,.49)],.012,EDGE)
# Modest central carved floral relief.
for i in range(7):
    a=2*math.pi*i/7
    chaise.include('apron_rosette_'+str(i),
       ball(.025,center=(.08+.064*math.cos(a),-.557,.49+.037*math.sin(a)),color=EDGE))
scene.include('chaise',chaise)

# Cropped foreground chair: cane seat, frame, and a little side rail.
chair = Asset('Foreground_cane_chair')
chair.include('seat_base',box((.71,.70,.065),center=(-1.63,-1.90,.45),color=FRAME))
for y in [-2.25,-1.55]:
    chair.include('rail_'+str(y),box((.79,.045,.065),center=(-1.63,y,.49),color=EDGE))
for x in [-2.02,-1.24]:
    chair.include('side_'+str(x),box((.05,.74,.065),center=(x,-1.90,.49),color=FRAME))
tube(chair,'curved_back_visible',[(-2.02,-1.55,.49),(-2.05,-1.55,.63),
     (-2.08,-1.55,.82)],.025,FRAME)
scene.include('foreground_chair',chair)

realize(scene)
sc=bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world=bpy.data.worlds.new('AmbientWorld')
sc.world.use_nodes=True
sc.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[0].default_value=(.72,.75,.78,1)
sc.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[1].default_value=.32

def material(name,color,roughness=.75):
    m=bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.diffuse_color=(*color,1)
    m.use_nodes=True
    p=m.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    p.inputs['Base Color'].default_value=(*color,1)
    p.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=roughness
    return m

fabric=material('Ivory woven fabric with faded rose stripes',(.84,.79,.67))
n=fabric.node_tree.nodes; l=fabric.node_tree.links
p=n.get('Principled BSDF')
tex=n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
sep=n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); l.new(tex.outputs['Generated'],sep.inputs[0])
wave=n.new('ShaderNodeTexWave'); wave.wave_type='BANDS'; wave.bands_direction='Y'
wave.inputs['Scale'].default_value=28
wave.inputs['Distortion'].default_value=.3
l.new(tex.outputs['Generated'],wave.inputs['Vector'])
r=n.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
r.color_ramp.elements.remove(r.color_ramp.elements[1])
for pos,col in [(0,(.78,.72,.61,1)),(.36,(.89,.84,.73,1)),
                (.78,(.88,.83,.72,1)),(.86,(.64,.43,.40,1)),(.91,(.87,.81,.69,1))]:
    e=r.color_ramp.elements[0] if pos==0 else r.color_ramp.elements.new(pos)
    e.color=col
l.new(wave.outputs['Fac'],r.inputs[0]); l.new(r.outputs[0],p.inputs['Base Color'])
noise=n.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise'); noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value=190
l.new(tex.outputs['Generated'],noise.inputs['Vector'])
bump=n.new('ShaderNodeBump'); bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.17
bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value=.009
l.new(noise.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height']); l.new(bump.outputs[0],p.inputs['Normal'])
plain=material('Pillow warm ivory',(.88,.82,.69))
n=plain.node_tree.nodes; l=plain.node_tree.links
no=n.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise'); no.inputs['Scale'].default_value=95
bu=n.new('ShaderNodeBump'); bu.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.23
bu.inputs['Distance'].default_value=.012
l.new(no.outputs['Fac'],bu.inputs['Height'])
l.new(bu.outputs[0],n.get('Principled BSDF').inputs['Normal'])

def parent_obj(name):
    return bpy.data.objects.get(name)

def mesh_obj(name,vertices,faces,mat,parent=None):
    me=bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    me.from_pydata(vertices,[],faces); me.update()
    ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,me); sc.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.data.materials.append(mat)
    if parent: ob.parent=parent
    return ob

# Extruded solid fabric panels; their broad surfaces remain visible inside rails.
def panel(name,outline,y,thickness):
    verts=[(x,y+dy,z) for dy in [-thickness/2,thickness/2] for x,z in outline]
    N=len(outline)
    faces=[tuple(range(N-1,-1,-1)),tuple(range(N,2*N))]
    faces += [(i,(i+1)%N,(i+1)%N+N,i+N) for i in range(N)]
    ob=mesh_obj(name,verts,faces,fabric,parent_obj('chaise'))
    be=ob.modifiers.new('Soft upholstery edges','BEVEL'); be.width=.022; be.segments=3
    ob.modifiers.new('Weighted upholstery normals','WEIGHTED_NORMAL')
    return ob
for y in [-.501,.47]:
    panel('Filled upholstered wing '+str(y),wing_outline,y,.055)

# Head panel curves across the full width behind the pillow.
verts=[]
for dz in [0,1]:
    for x,y,z in head_top:
        verts.append((x+.025,y,.62 if dz==0 else z-.035))
N=len(head_top)
faces=[(i,i+1,N+i+1,N+i) for i in range(N-1)]
head=mesh_obj('Broad upholstered head',verts,faces,fabric,parent_obj('chaise'))
sol=head.modifiers.new('Padded head thickness','SOLIDIFY'); sol.thickness=.09
be=head.modifiers.new('Head softness','BEVEL'); be.width=.035; be.segments=3

# Rounded continuous mattress with a gently domed top and rounded foot end.
verts=[]; faces=[]; count=64
for z,sx,sy in [(.61,.95,.92),(.66,1,1),(.76,.99,.98),(.795,.91,.88)]:
    for i in range(count):
        a=2*math.pi*i/count
        c,s=math.cos(a),math.sin(a)
        x=.005+1.345*sx*math.copysign(abs(c)**.40,c)
        y=.515*sy*math.copysign(abs(s)**.44,s)
        verts.append((x,y,z))
for j in range(3):
    for i in range(count):
        faces.append((j*count+i,j*count+(i+1)%count,
                      (j+1)*count+(i+1)%count,(j+1)*count+i))
faces.append(tuple(range(3*count,4*count)))
faces.append(tuple(range(count-1,-1,-1)))
seat=mesh_obj('Continuous upholstered seat cushion',verts,faces,fabric,parent_obj('chaise'))
for f in seat.data.polygons: f.use_smooth=True
seat.modifiers.new('Cushion weighted normals','WEIGHTED_NORMAL')

def soft_cube(name,loc,size,mat,bevel=.06,rotation=(0,0,0),parent=None):

    ob=bpy.context.object; ob.name=name
    ob.dimensions=size
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False,rotation=False,scale=True)
    ob.rotation_euler=rotation
    ob.data.materials.append(mat)
    be=ob.modifiers.new('Rounded sewn edges','BEVEL')
    be.width=bevel; be.segments=5
    ob.modifiers.new('Weighted normals','WEIGHTED_NORMAL')
    if parent: ob.parent=parent
    return ob

curve.bevel_depth=.006; curve.bevel_resolution=2
spline=curve.splines.new('POLY'); spline.points.add(8)
for p,co in zip(spline.points,[(.135,-.29,-.31),(.135,0,-.34),(.135,.29,-.31),
    (.135,.33,0),(.135,.29,.31),(.135,0,.34),(.135,-.29,.31),
    (.135,-.33,0),(.135,-.29,-.31)]):
    p.co=(*co,1)
ob=bpy.data.objects.new('Pillow sewn perimeter',curve); sc.collection.objects.link(ob)
ob.data.materials.append(seam_mat); ob.parent=pillow

labelmat=material('Dark green exhibit label',(.035,.18,.145))
label=soft_cube('Small green label',(.77,.13,.803),(.105,.225,.008),labelmat,.004,
                (0,0,math.radians(-8)),parent_obj('chaise'))
ink=material('Label cream print',(.76,.79,.65))
for i in range(3):
    soft_cube('Label printed stroke '+str(i),(.77,.105+i*.025,.809),
              (.055 if i==0 else .034,.004,.0015),ink,.0005,parent=parent_obj('chaise'))

# Window curtain, mostly cropped along the left border.
curtainmat=material('Curtain soft linen',(.83,.80,.71))
sheer=material('Bright window voile',(.96,.94,.86))
for index,(cx,mat,width) in enumerate([(-2.02,curtainmat,.35),(-2.26,sheer,.30)]):
    vv=[]; ff=[]; steps=24
    for z in [.02,2.9]:
        for i in range(steps+1):
            x=cx+width*(i/steps-.5)
            y=.35+.045*math.cos(i*math.pi*2/4)
            vv.append((x,y,z))
    for i in range(steps):
        ff.append((i,i+1,steps+i+2,steps+i+1))
    ob=mesh_obj('Hanging curtain '+str(index),vv,ff,mat)
    so=ob.modifiers.new('Linen thickness','SOLIDIFY'); so.thickness=.007

# Parquet reads as broad dark wooden regions with fine plank seams.
